section: E-invoicing in Germany (E-Rechnung, XRechnung and ZUGFeRD)
wording: When a German business must issue an e-invoice, when a paper or PDF invoice is still allowed, what every business must be able to receive, which formats count, how to correct, check and store e-invoices, and how invoicing federal authorities differs. It is for businesses, freelancers, landlords and associations in Germany, for foreign businesses that invoice German customers, and for the people who keep their books. Figures are for tax year 2026. The rules are read from the consolidated federal law pages (UStG, UStDV, AO, ERechV), from the finance ministry's letter of 15 October 2025, which writes the e-invoice rules into the VAT application decree (Umsatzsteuer-Anwendungserlass), from the ministry's questions and answers page (as of March 2026), and from the GoBD change letters of 11 March 2024 and 14 July 2025. The reduced VAT rate is printed as a digit only in the ministry's tax booklet, 2025 edition; the statute states it in words. The ministry's first e-invoice letter, of 15 October 2024, is no longer at its address on the ministry's site, so nothing in this Guide rests on it alone.

wording: - **Two dates and the default duty: selected combined-law interpretation.** Each § 27(38) relief tests both the supply date and the last transmission date. For an ordinary taxable domestic business-to-business supply made in December 2026, first invoiced in January 2027, the default § 14(2) e-invoice duty applies if both parties meet the domestic-establishment test, the recipient acquires for its business, the invoice total is above EUR 250, and no Kleinunternehmer, ticket or other permanent exemption applies. This fixture assumes no previously issued qualifying advance or standing invoice; those follow their specific rules below. No. 1 relief ended on 31 December 2026; nos. 2 and 3 concern supplies made after that date, so neither low issuer turnover nor the December supply date rescues this January invoice. This is a labelled reading of the own default and transition clauses, not a separate ruling. The same December supply first sent by 31 December 2026 can use paper or an agreed PDF under no. 1. A supply made on 1 January 2027 instead enters no. 2's own prior-year-turnover test and 2027 transmission window. The ministry applies the principles to post-2024 supplies, subject to the actual transition. Reapply these exact duty/relief gates to other late invoices rather than inferring a gap in all invoicing rules.

wording: - **Hybrid files: the XML leads.** Before 2025 the picture part led. Now the structured part is the leading part, and if the two differ the structured data decide (decree section 14.4(3); questions and answers, no. 12a).
